name: The Ancestor's Knucklebone
object: A knucklebone worn smooth by a hundred years of handling, threaded on gut string. Taken from the body of a Berserker who died fighting in the Borderlands and was never retrieved. It arrived in a collector's satchel through one of the Market Square arches, and nobody knows which world it came from, or who carried it through.
unlock: Defeat an enemy in single combat without any ally's assistance.
Keep one of the body's hand bones.
Spend a night alone with it before you sleep, and see how the ancestor fought.
risk: At dawn, make a WIL save, DC 12. On a failure, the ancestor's last fight plays out in you: take 1 Wound you do not remember taking, and whatever hunted them learns where you sleep.

resource.name: Fury Echo
resource.text: Fury Echo (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Fury Echo each time you tell a listener who has not heard it how the ancestor fought and fell, in full, over at least ten minutes. Echo never clears at a rest or when combat ends. Spent Echo returns only by telling it again to a new listener.

powers: Echo Strike (Free, while Raging, spend 1 Fury Echo): Roll a Fury Die and set it aside with the rest, up to your maximum. This does not use your Rage action.
Death's Door (Free, 1/encounter, when you Rage, spend all 3 Fury Echo): For this encounter, your Rage does not end when you drop to 0 HP. Dying applies as normal.
escalation: If you drop to 0 HP with Death's Door active, the knucklebone cracks and stops working. Replace it with another ancestor's relic from the Borderlands, or take one from a worthy enemy. The GM decides where it is and how long the search takes. Whatever hunted the ancestor learns the bone has moved.

name: The Loaded Die
object: An ivory gambling die with a tiny lead insert that makes it land on 6 roughly two-thirds of the time. Confiscated from a Black Hand card sharp at the Lower Reaches gambling house, then stolen from the evidence shelf at the Golden Knights' outpost. No paperwork exists for it. The card sharp has not stopped looking.
unlock: Win a wager against someone who genuinely believed they had the advantage: not a mark, not a fool, but someone who should have won.
Stake something you cannot afford to lose.
risk: After the wager, the loser rolls Insight against your Influence roll. If they win, they know the die was loaded, and they name you to the Black Hand card sharp.

resource.name: Fixes
resource.text: Fixes (pip tracker, max 4). Fixes do not refill automatically. To refill: run a game of chance during a Safe Rest and earn at least 1 silver in genuine winnings against an opponent who had a real chance of winning. Gain all 4 Fixes back. Safe Rests where you do not gamble leave the tracker as it is. Fixes return only this way.

powers: Fix (Free, before you roll, spend 1 Fix): Declare you are using the die. Roll your Primary Die twice and take whichever result you prefer. No memory required, both rolls happen now, in front of everyone.
Loaded Odds (Passive): Once per session, you may ask the GM whether a creature you can see is bluffing. The die rolls and the GM answers truthfully, but only yes or no.
escalation: When all 4 Fixes are spent, the die gets you anyway. On your next Vicious Opportunist use after depletion, the GM secretly decides whether the target was actually Distracted, and you do not know until after you have committed. The uncertainty lasts for one use only. Word that a loaded die is back in play reaches the card sharp within a session.

name: The Battle Standard of the Nameless King
object: A black iron battle standard, the insignia ground off but the pole still bearing ghost-traces of a name no one can read. Found stacked with other confiscated relics in the Museum of Worlds Beyond storage vault. The curator is looking for it. Three scholars have separately attempted to identify the insignia's origin and stopped work without explanation.
unlock: Lead a group of at least five non-party combatants to victory: soldiers, militia, hired swords, anyone you commanded in the field. The victory must be real, a fight that could have been lost.
Plant the standard yourself, in plain sight of the enemy.
risk: The first time you plant it, roll a d6. On a 1-3, someone in the watching crowd or the enemy ranks recognizes the standard, and the Knights of the Nameless King send an agent within two sessions.

resource.name: Authority
resource.text: Authority (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Authority whenever an ally within 4 spaces of the planted standard deals damage in a single attack equal to or greater than your level. Authority is strictly encounter-bound: all unspent pips are lost when combat ends, regardless of how many are held. It cannot be saved or stockpiled between encounters.

powers: Plant it (1 Action): Drive the standard into the ground within Reach 1. While it stands, allies within 4 spaces who can see it have advantage on their first attack each round. Spend 1 Authority to extend the aura by 2 spaces until your next turn.
Pull it (Free): The standard returns to your hand and the aura ends immediately.
Hold Ground (Reaction, spend 2 Authority): When the standard would be knocked over, stolen, or destroyed, it refuses. It cannot be moved by any force until the start of your next turn.
escalation: When Authority is at 0 during combat and you plant the standard anyway, the insignia becomes briefly legible to everyone present. The GM reads what it says aloud. It goes dark again immediately. What it says is the GM's tool: a name, a title, a command. Prepare it before the session.

name: The Borderlands Tracking Cord
object: A length of braided sinew hung with small carved tokens: a boot print, a feather, a fang, and three others worn unrecognisable by handling. Carried by a tracker from the Doorish Hills who traded it to a Lower Reaches merchant for safe passage through the Cliffs of the Dead. The merchant did not survive the arrangement.
unlock: Track a single creature across at least two sessions without losing the trail, through city, ruin, or wilderness. The creature must be aware it is being hunted, and must have tried to lose you at least once.
risk: Each session you track the creature, the GM rolls a d6. On a 1, it doubles back and ambushes you, and it acts first in the next encounter.

resource.name: Marks
resource.text: Marks (d6 vs. accumulation). Your Mark count is the number of quarries the cord currently tracks. Roll 1d6 each time you use a cord ability (Mark a Quarry or Cord Pull). If you roll equal to or below your current Mark count, something near the quarry noticed you. A Mark clears when you confront that quarry directly or when you Cut its Mark. Resting does not clear Marks.

powers: Mark a Quarry (1 Action): Touch the cord to any physical trace of a creature: a footprint, a drop of blood, shed skin. Add 1 Mark. While that quarry is marked, you know its general direction and distance within 1 mile regardless of cover or concealment. This works on creatures you have not marked with Hunter's Mark, because the cord marks independently of the class ability.
Cord Pull (Free, 1/encounter): When your marked quarry moves away from you, pull the cord taut. The quarry is Slowed. No roll required. The quarry feels it.

Cut the Mark (Free): Remove one Mark from the cord and burn its token. The cord forgets that quarry, your sense of its direction ends, and it is no longer tracked. Use this when the pursuit is no longer worth the rising risk. Nothing alerts the quarry.
escalation: When the d6 roll triggers, the quarry, or something near it, begins tracking you in return. The GM introduces this threat within 1 to 2 sessions. The threat is proportional to what you marked: a city rat sends a rat, a Borderlands warlord sends soldiers.

name: The Cracked Lens of Kartan
object: A monocle lens of blue glass, cracked through the centre but held in a copper frame that prevents the crack from spreading. Stamped with the Mages of Kartan's maker's mark on the inner rim. The Mages report it stolen. It has been in a Lower Reaches pawn shop for six months, priced too high for anyone who recognised it, too strange for anyone who didn't.
unlock: Pay the pawn shop's price, which is more than the lens is worth.
Spend a week of downtime studying the crack through the lens, and make an Arcana check, DC 12, to read the maker's mark. On a failure the week is spent and you start over.
Then cast a spell of the highest tier you can cast, with the lens held to your eye for the whole cast.
risk: Roll a d6 when the cast ends. On a 1-2 the lens fails as its Escalation describes: take 1 Wound, the lens fuses to your face until the encounter ends, and Kartan is told. On a 3 or higher it bonds. If you flinch or remove the lens, the crack spreads and it is ruined.

resource.name: Overcharge
resource.text: Overcharge (d6 vs. accumulation). Roll 1d6 each time you cast a tiered spell while wearing the lens. If you roll equal to or below your current Overcharge, the lens fails (see Escalation). Overcharge clears when you hold the lens to the glass of the Observatory of Infinite Skies through one night.

powers: Controlled Upcast (while worn, on a safe roll, Control subclass only): When you cast a tiered spell and the d6 does not trigger, the spell gains one Upcast for free. Add 1 Overcharge. Chaos subclass: no upcast. On a safe roll, reduce Overcharge by 1 (minimum 0).

Chaos Sight (Passive, while worn): You see magical auras on creatures and objects within 4 spaces without casting a spell. Illusions appear slightly wrong. Invisible creatures show as a faint shimmer.
escalation: When the d6 triggers, the glass heats to burning. Control Mage: you Lose Control, doing every option on the Control Table, with the GM choosing each time. Chaos Mage: you Invoke Chaos with disadvantage. Either way you take 1 Wound and cannot remove the lens until the encounter ends, because it has fused to your face. After the encounter, the Mages of Kartan sense the discharge and know its rough location. They send someone within 1 to 3 sessions. The fusing is now, the visitors are later.

name: The Broken Verdict
object: A set of golden scales, one pan snapped off and missing. Recovered from the rubble of an old court in the ruins of Sunken Revvia. The remaining pan still tilts when a lie is spoken nearby, or so the merchant who sold it claimed. She may have been lying. The tilt is subtle enough that you cannot always be certain.
unlock: Refuse to deliver a verdict you believe is just, because doing so would protect someone you love.
The refusal must be genuine. The Verdict will know if you were simply afraid.
risk: The GM starts a six-step clock for whoever was owed the verdict. It ticks whenever you are seen shielding the person you chose, and when it fills they act against you both.

resource.name: Held Judgment
resource.text: Held Judgment (toggle, on/off). When your Radiant Judgment would roll Judgment Dice, you may put them on the scales instead, which turns the toggle on. While the scales hold dice, you roll no new Judgment Dice. Held dice stay on the scales past the end of the encounter. The toggle clears when you Release the dice on an attack, or when you perform a Sacred Decree (see Escalation).

powers: Hold Judgment (Free, when Judgment Dice would be rolled): Keep the dice on the scales. While they are held, you see the remaining pan tilt when a creature within 6 spaces lies to you, visible only to you. You know. They do not know you know. You must decide what to do with that.
Release (Free, 1/encounter, on a Reach attack): Expend the held dice as Radiant Judgment normally does. This attack's radiant damage ignores armor.
escalation: If the scales hold dice through a full Safe Rest, they fuse with your Lay on Hands pool. You cannot spend from the pool until you perform a Sacred Decree at the Temple of the Three Sisters. The temple will want to know why.

name: The Hollow Contract
object: A slip of black vellum the size of a playing card, written in a language that changes every time you look away. No ink is visible: the text appears to be burned into the material from within. Found pressed between the floorboards of a sealed room in the Lower Reaches, below a building that has been empty for eleven years. The landlord will not say why.
unlock: Patron path: commune with your patron during a Safe Rest and ask it for something you know it does not want to give. Accept its counter-demand before you know what it is.
Reaver path: you have no patron to ask. Read the vellum by your own shadow, in the room where it was found, for three nights, until the language stops changing.
risk: Patron path: the counter-demand is whatever the GM names, and you have already agreed to it. Reaver path: make a WIL save, DC 12, each night, and each failure starts you with 1 Debt before you have any power. Either way, your patron, or the patron you left, learns the contract has a new reader.

resource.name: Debt
resource.text: Debt (pip tracker, max 4). Mark 1 Debt each time you use one of the contract's powers. Debt clears when the patron collects (see Escalation), or when you carry out a sentence you wrote in the contract: write one sentence in your own blood describing something you will do for the patron, then do it. You must write something real, and you must mean it.

powers: Read the Contract (Free, 1/encounter, mark 1 Debt): Hold the vellum up. You see one true fact about a creature you can see: its most urgent want, its deepest fear, or the name of someone it has wronged.
Patron's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, patron path): Cast one tiered spell you know at +1 tier above your current maximum. The patron extends credit.
Reaver's Margin (Free, 1/encounter, mark 2 Debt, Reaver path): Your next Bonescythe strike this turn rolls 1 extra damage die.
escalation: When Debt reaches 4, the patron collects. It does not take power. It adds one sentence about your character to the contract, permanently. The GM decides what it says and reads it aloud. Debt clears. The sentence stays. A Reaver's former patron sends an agent to read the sentence to them in person.

name: The Bell of the Three Sisters
object: A small iron handbell, tarnished green at the rim, engraved with three interlinked rings. Identical to the bells carried by the clergy of the Temple of the Three Sisters, except that this one rings slightly differently, a half-note flat or sharp depending on who you ask. The temple says it was never consecrated. They are interested in recovering it for study. They have not offered to pay.
unlock: Heal a creature you expected, and had good reason, to be your enemy, spending healing that an ally needed.
The expectation must be genuine. The bell listens.
risk: The first time you ring it at the Temple of the Three Sisters, the clergy ask who consecrated it. Make an Influence check, DC 14, to answer without lying. On a failure they take the bell for study until you run an errand for them.

resource.name: Resonance
resource.text: Resonance (pip tracker, max 4). Gain 1 Resonance by ringing the bell for an hour over a sickbed or a grave, at the Temple of the Three Sisters or among the tombs of the Cliffs of the Dead, and staying with whoever it is for until the hour ends. Resonance does not clear at a rest. Spent Resonance returns only this way.

powers: Ring Out (Free, spend 1 Resonance): One Dying ally within 6 spaces hears the bell. On its next turn it acts as if it were not Dying: no 1-action limit, and no STR save to attack.

Chain Heal (Reaction, spend 2 Resonance): When your Lifebinding Spirit heals a creature to maximum HP, the excess healing carries to the nearest damaged ally within 4 spaces. The chain triggers once per Reaction.
Toll (1 Action, spend all 4): Ring the bell loudly. All Dying allies within 6 spaces gain 1 HP and are no longer Dying. You take 1 Wound.
escalation: Spending all 4 Resonance in the Toll cracks the bell's handle. It still rings, but you cannot Toll until a clergyperson of the Three Sisters rehandles it. They will want to know what happened before they agree to help.

name: The Theater of Whispers Setlist
object: A folded sheet of vellum with a handwritten set of songs: titles, keys, and performance notes in the margins in an elegant hand. It belonged to a Songweaver who performed at the Theater of Whispers for fifteen years before disappearing mid-run. The theater kept the setlist. Someone stole it last month. The manager has posted a reward, but is vaguer than expected about what they want to do with whoever took it.
unlock: Perform at the Theater of Whispers, or any venue with an audience of 20 or more, and hold the crowd's full attention for an uninterrupted hour. No skill check. Just perform.
Find someone who heard the setlist's owner perform, and learn the last song, which has no title.
risk: Roll a d6 when the hour ends. On a 1-2, someone in that crowd knows the hand that wrote the setlist, and they find you within a session.

resource.name: Crowd
resource.text: Crowd (d6 vs. accumulation, max 4). Each time you Call the Song in combat, roll 1d6 against your current Crowd, then add 1 Crowd. If you roll equal to or below your Crowd before adding, someone recognises the song and has feelings about it: you have disadvantage on your next social roll with a stranger this session. Crowd clears when you play a full uninterrupted hour for a new audience of 20 or more.

powers: Call the Song (Free, in combat, 1/round): Name the song you are playing and roll against your Crowd. On a safe roll, you regain 1 spent use of Songweaver's Inspiration. This works once per encounter.
Protective Verse (Free, 1/encounter, remove 2 Crowd): A specific song from the setlist grants immunity to the Taunted or Frightened condition to all allies within 6 spaces until the end of the round.
escalation: When Crowd reaches 4, someone in the crowd knows who this setlist belonged to. They approach between encounters, or send someone. The GM decides who and what they want. They may be a fan. They may not.

name: Mud from the Revlend Marshes
object: A sealed clay jar of dark grey mud from the Revlend Marshes north of the city, marked with protective runes no one recognises as any known system. The mud is warm to the touch and smells of rain before a storm. It never dries out. An arch-traveller carried it into the city claiming the marshes spoke to her. She didn't explain further. She is not currently available to explain anything.
unlock: Spend a full night alone in the Revlend Marshes, or in the Deadlands adjacent to them, without shelter or fire.
Something in the marshes must acknowledge you before dawn. You will know if it did.
risk: At dawn, make a WIL save, DC 13. On a failure, the marshes keep something small from you (the GM names it: your first name, the color of your eyes, the sound of your laugh) until you carry the jar back and refill it.

resource.name: Earthpulse
resource.text: Earthpulse (pip tracker, max 4). The jar holds 4 Earthpulse when it is full. Using the mud spends Earthpulse (see Powers). Spent Earthpulse returns only when you carry the jar back to the Revlend Marshes and leave it there overnight. A rest does not refill it.

powers: Apply (1 Action, spend 1 Earthpulse): Smear the mud on yourself or a willing creature. While it is applied, the creature cannot be pushed, thrown, or moved by non-magical forced movement. Mud washes off in rain or after a Field Rest.
Extend the Beastshift (Free, spend 2 Earthpulse, once per Beastshift): Your Beastshift does not end when you cast a spell this encounter.

Mire (1 Action, spend all 4): Create a 3-space radius of difficult terrain centered on you that lasts until the end of the encounter. The ground thickens and pulls. Any creature that starts its turn in the mire is Slowed.
escalation: When the jar is empty, mud already applied does not dry, but no new mud can be applied until the jar is refilled. If the jar breaks, the mud it held dries at once and all its effects end. A skilled craftsperson can repair a broken jar, but the marshes must still refill it. Each time you return to refill it, the marshes have changed, and the GM says how.

name: The Pain Teacher's Wrappings
object: Linen hand wrappings, yellowed and stained, covered in faded ink annotations, technique notes in a script that predates the city. Found in a locked case in the Lower Reaches beneath a martial arts studio that has been occupied by different teachers for four centuries. Each teacher added their own notes in the margins. The last teacher's annotations stop mid-sentence, mid-technique.
unlock: Study the wrappings' first annotation for a week of downtime.

Then take a hit in combat that you could have Defended but deliberately chose not to, in order to observe how the attack was made. The choice must be your own. The wrappings can tell the difference between courage and negligence.
risk: If the hit drops you to 0 HP, the wrappings do not count it. You take the Wound and must try again after you recover. The last teacher's notes stop mid-technique, and whoever silenced them hears the wrappings are in use.

resource.name: Strain
resource.text: Strain (Wound-cost). Each annotation you use costs 1 Wound. There is no tracker, only the Wounds. A Medical Kit, healing magic and other effects cannot remove these Wounds; they heal only by Safe Rest, 1 per rest.

powers: Study the Form (Free, spend 1 Wound, 1/encounter): Before you attack a creature, spend 1 Wound to activate the wrappings' oldest annotations. For the rest of the encounter, your attacks against that creature ignore its armor. You are choosing to hurt yourself to learn faster.
Deepest Annotation (Free, spend 1 Wound, 1/Safe Rest): Your unarmed and martial weapon attacks deal bonus damage equal to your level for 1 minute.

Study (downtime, 1 hour per Safe Rest): Spend an hour reading the annotations during rest. Roll Lore DC 8 to learn something about a martial tradition relevant to the current adventure arc. The GM provides one true detail.
escalation: If you use either annotation while you have 3 or more Wounds, from any source, the wrappings tighten around your hands: take 1 additional Wound and you cannot use either annotation for 1 round. The annotations become illegible until a skilled martial artist re-inks them. Finding one is the GM's hook.

name: The Forgotten Key
object: A tarnished iron key, not sized for any human lock. Found in rubble beneath the Theater of Whispers, its bow etched with a spiral that matches no arch in the city's records.
unlock: Present it to each of the city's seven major arches while the Archkeepers watch
Find the one arch that hums
Spend a full night at its threshold
risk: The arch opens briefly. Roll a d6: on a 1-2, something comes through before you close the way. Closing it takes a Lore check, DC 12.

resource.name: Hum
resource.text: Hum (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Hum each time you Open the Way. Regain 1 when you carry the key to an arch you have not yet tried it on and an Archkeeper records what the arch did. Hum never returns at a rest.

powers: Open the Way (Action, spend 1 Hum): A dormant arch opens for up to a minute. Make a Lore check, DC 12, or you cannot control where it leads. A crit lets you sense the destination first.
Tuning (Passive): The key hums faintly within 6 spaces of a dormant arch.
escalation: Spending the last Hum, roll a d6. On 1-2 the key splinters, and every arch it opens leads somewhere wrong until an Archkeeper repairs it. On 3+, take 1 Wound.

name: The Drowning Scale
object: A cold, clammy pendant on a leather cord, a single shimmering scale of unknown origin. When first worn, everyone nearby shivers. It was pulled from the water at Drowned Elvenya in the Revlend Marshes, and nobody knows what it came off.
unlock: Wear the pendant ceaselessly for a full lunar cycle, answering its whispered questions honestly each night
Hold yourself underwater until you genuinely risk drowning
risk: Make a STR save, DC 14, or take 1 Wound. Each night's honest answer is a secret the GM may make true in the fiction.

resource.name: Breath
resource.text: Breath (pip tracker, max 4). Gain 1 Breath each time you draw a creature's last breath (see Last Breath). All Breath is lost when you take the pendant off. A rest does not clear it.

powers: Last Breath (Reaction, 1/round): When a creature within Reach 2 drops to 0 HP, you draw its last breath and gain 1 Breath. Make a WIL save, DC 12, or gain a Condition of the GM's choice from Frightened, Dazed or Slowed until the end of your next turn.
Cold Skin (Passive): While you hold any Breath, you are immune to cold damage and to the dangers of extreme cold.
Hold the Breath (Free, spend 1 Breath): You go without air for up to one hour.
Choke (1 Action, spend 2 Breath): A creature within Reach 2 gasps. It makes a STR save, DC 13, or is Incapacitated as it chokes, until the end of its next turn. The whispers tell you its name.
escalation: If you try to use the pendant with no Breath, make a WIL save, DC 12, or you inhale your own breath: take 1 Wound and become Dying at once.

name: The Axe of Nine Eyes
object: A silvery greataxe with nine open eyes engraved down the blade. They follow whoever speaks. It came out of Graydust Keep, which has changed hands hundreds of times since the fall of the Nameless King, and the Fallen Angels who hold the keep now want it back.
unlock: Learn what the axe was called before it was named, from Archkeeper records or something older than the Golden Order
Let it name a creature in a room you thought was empty
Hold the line against that creature until it flees or dies
risk: The creature's side now knows your name, and the GM starts a six-step clock for them.

resource.name: Eyes
resource.text: Eyes (finite, 9). Each Name It closes one eye. A closed eye never reopens, and nothing refills the axe.

powers: Name It (Action, spend 1 Eye): Choose one creature you can see. You learn its True Name and have advantage on checks against it.
Named (Passive): You always know the direction and distance of any creature you have Named.
Speak the Name (Reaction, 1/encounter): A Named creature loses its next action. WIL DC 14 negates; Solo creatures save with advantage.
escalation: Named creatures learn your name and heading each dawn. When the ninth eye closes, the axe speaks your True Name and all nine hear it. One engraved eye is scraped blank.

name: The Hourglass of Borrowed Time
object: A brass hourglass whose sand climbs upward. The Library of Vrassa has no record of lending it, and no record of getting it back.
unlock: Watch one full night without sleeping
Tell an NPC, truthfully, the moment you would undo
risk: The sand climbs for a stranger first. They relive their last hour, and they remember you. Make a WIL save, DC 12, or the hour comes out of your own life: lose 1 Hit Die until your next Safe Rest.

resource.name: Sand
resource.text: Sand (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Sand each time you Turn Back. Regain 1 by returning to the place where you last turned time back and letting the glass run for an hour. Sand returns only this way.

powers: Turn Back (Reaction, spend 1 Sand): Any die roll you can see is rerolled. The new result stands.
Sand Sense (Passive): You always know the exact time, and you can tell when a clock, a calendar, or a witness near you has it wrong.
escalation: When the last Sand falls, the original result happened somewhere. Within a session an Echo of you arrives carrying its consequences, and it wants the glass.

name: The Black Lotus Case
object: A black bloom pressed in a lead-lined case, three petals left, still damp. According to the trader who sold it, it was cut at the Oasis of Mother's Tears in the Deadlands.
unlock: Find someone who survived the preparation
Fast three days
Eat the first petal under watch
risk: WIL DC 14 or take 2 Wounds, and the Stain advances now.

resource.name: Petals
resource.text: Petals (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Petal each time you eat one. Regain 1 by seeding the bloom where someone you knew died and tending the soil for a week. Petals return only this way.

powers: Eat a Petal (Action, spend 1 Petal): Choose one of the three effects below. It lasts an encounter.
Smoke Step (Free, 1/round, while chosen): Teleport to a spot you can see within 6 spaces.
Wallwalker (Passive, while chosen): Climb sheer surfaces and walk on water.
Drowsing Pollen (once, when chosen): One creature of level 5 or lower within 2 spaces makes a WIL save, DC 13, or falls asleep for 1d4 rounds.
escalation: Each time the case empties, the Stain advances for good. 1: fingertips blacken, advantage on Finesse, and you can no longer feel heat or cold through them. 2: veins darken, +1 Initiative, your pulse is audible. 3: eyes black, you see in the dark, strangers flinch (disadvantage on Influence). After 3, the bloom no longer needs the case.

name: The Oath-Band
object: A plain iron ring, every oath ever sworn over it scratched inside. The first is in the hand of a Golden Knights recruit, and the Citadel has no record of the ring.
unlock: Swear aloud before a living witness
The oath must be something you would not otherwise do and will take at least a full session to fulfil; the GM may refuse one that matches your plans
risk: The Band holds your words, not your meaning. The GM may close loopholes, and when they do the oath is graded one step higher. If you then fail it, you lose the higher grade's max HP.

resource.name: Oath
resource.text: Oath (toggle, max 1). Set when you swear. Clears when you fulfil the oath, or when the GM rules it broken or abandoned. One oath at a time, and a new one only after the last has cleared.

powers: Sworn (Passive): While the oath stands, you have advantage on checks that directly advance it. The GM grades it Worthy, Mighty or Legendary when you swear.
Hold Fast (Reaction, once per oath): When you fail a check or save that directly advances the oath, reroll it with advantage. The oath drops one grade.
escalation: Fulfilled: heal 1 Wound and gain +1, +2 or +3 max HP for good, by grade. Failed: lose that much max HP for good, the Golden Council writes the broken oath on the record under your name, and the Band stays shut until you do a penance.

name: The Unpaid Favor
object: A tin holy symbol, its face rubbed smooth, always warm. It belongs to one of the twelve profane gods of the Temple of the Lower Twelve, and the face has been rubbed past telling which.
unlock: Learn which of the Lower Twelve it belongs to
Make a true offering at midnight
risk: The patron takes a small price first. Make a WIL save, DC 12. On a success it takes only your name for a week. On a failure it takes a memory, and the GM names which.

resource.name: Tithe
resource.text: Tithe (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Tithe each time you Call In. Tithe clears only when you do the patron a favor the GM presents.

powers: Call In (Action, +1 Tithe): One small, specific impossibility. A door opens, a lie is believed, or a creature within 6 spaces loses its next action (WIL save, DC 13, negates).
Warm (Passive): The symbol grows hot when a worshipper of the Lower Twelve is within 6 spaces.
escalation: If you Call In with 3 Tithe, the patron collects first. Roll a d6. 1 Newt: tiny and actionless for 3 rounds. 2 Imps: lose 2 random items. 3 Salt ring: you cannot cross it until it breaks. 4 Cobwebs: no arcanum use until you atone. 5 Nemesis: someone is born who will hunt you. 6 Wither: take 1 Wound.

name: The Valkyrie's Feather
object: A gold-barbed feather from a warrior's grave on the far side of an arch, in a world where valkyries still collect the dead.
unlock: Dig it from the grave
Learn the warrior's story
risk: 1 in 20 the valkyrie comes for the grave-robber before you finish.

resource.name: Tally
resource.text: Tally (d6 vs. accumulation). Add 1 Tally each time you use Spared, then roll a d6. If it rolls equal to or under your Tally, a valkyrie comes for the spared life (see Escalation). Tally clears only when you carry the feather back to its stone in the grave it came from.

powers: Spared (Reaction, 1/encounter, +1 Tally): You or an ally within 6 spaces stays at 1 HP instead of dropping to 0.
Gold Barbs (Passive): The barbs glow when a creature within 12 spaces drops to 0 HP.
escalation: A valkyrie arrives within a day to claim the spared life, yours or your ally's. She will hear one argument for it. The GM plays her.

name: The Tide-Coat
object: An eel-skin suit that covers you head to heel, crusted with barnacles. Underwater it hums.
unlock: Win it from the Revlenders of Heron's Stride or the people of a drowned place, or earn it in their service
Wear it for a full night underwater
risk: Something in the deep hears the hum. Roll a d6 at dawn: on a 1-2 it follows you up and arrives within a session.

resource.name: Growth
resource.text: Growth (pip tracker, max 4). Gain 1 Growth for each hour you spend underwater in a drowned place (the Lost Cisterns, Sunken Revvia, a flooded vault), beyond what the gig needs. That hour costs a scene. A rest never adds Growth. Lose 1 Growth when you take a Wound, and 1 each day after a week spent dry. Using Eel Slip spends 1 Growth.

powers: Tide Skin (Passive): Defense 3+DEX, plus 1 per Growth. Each Growth also gives -1 to Stealth.
Eel Slip (Reaction, spend 1 Growth): When you are Grappled or Restrained, you slip free and move 1 space.
escalation: At 4 Growth the coat is a landmark, and things in the deep start coming to see it.

name: The Pitch-Sap Harness
object: Three layers of wood glued with sap that never dries, its outer layer bristling with thorns. The wood was cut in the Lost Cavern of the Sundering Saurians, from a jungle tree that offered it, and it still smells of the mist.
unlock: Find an old tree in the Lost Cavern of the Sundering Saurians willing to give its sap
Wear it through one fight without taking it off
risk: The sap takes. It won't come off until the next full moon.

resource.name: Burden
resource.text: Burden (pip tracker, max 3), one per weapon stuck in the sap. Burden clears when you pry the stuck weapons loose, which takes tools and an hour, and then re-glue the harness with fresh sap from the tree that gave it. A Safe Rest does not clear Burden.

powers: Thorned Bark (Passive): Defense 6+DEX (max 2) and advantage on Stealth in forests and jungles. Each Burden gives -1 Speed.

Snare (Reaction, +1 Burden): When a melee weapon hits you, the attacker makes a STR save, DC 13, or the weapon sticks. A creature using natural weapons is Grappled to you until it passes the save, and adds no Burden.
escalation: When Burden would pass 3, the sap seals you in: you are Restrained until someone spends an action and passes a Might check, DC 14, to cut you out. Then the harness gives half its Defense until it is glued again with fresh sap.

name: The Hellhide
object: Plate made over with a demon's skin, its horns on the helm and its claws on the gauntlets. The skin came out of Irax, the wind-torn hell beyond the hidden archway of the Blood Spears' Watchtower of Averost.
unlock: Hunt the demon and bring back the skin
Find a smith who will work it, and pay their price
Put it on
risk: Roll d10. On 1-3 the hide drinks magic: no spell can affect you, including your own, while you wear it.

resource.name: Thirst
resource.text: Thirst (pip tracker, max 3). Gain 1 Thirst each time you use Command. Thirst clears only when you offer blood to the hide outside combat, from a creature that was not trying to harm you. Blood shed in a fight does not count.

powers: Demon Plate (Passive): Defense 14, with no STR requirement.
Terror (Passive): The first time a creature sees you in an encounter, it makes a WIL save, DC 14, or has -1 to all its rolls near you for the encounter.
Command (Action, +1 Thirst, 1/encounter): Order undead or a demon to obey one command.
escalation: You cannot willingly part with the hide, and you will hunt anyone who takes it. If you end a day with 3 Thirst, it drinks from you at dawn: take 1 Wound that cannot heal while you wear it. If you die in it, you rise as a spectre.

name: The Kettle Plate
object: Full plate with two boilers on the back and a servo at every joint. One of a kind, built to someone's measure, and not to yours. The boiler plate is stamped with the mark of Vathrex's Forge.
unlock: Find the workshop that built it
Have it refitted to you, which costs a favor the makers name
Stoke it yourself, the first time
risk: The refit fails on a test fire. 1d6 fire damage and a week of repairs.

resource.name: Steam
resource.text: Steam (pip tracker, max 4). Spend 1 Steam per use. Regain all by stoking the boilers with a load of forge coal drawn from Vathrex's Forge, which means a trip to the ziggurat and whatever price Erna Ironhorn names. A load fills the boilers once and takes an inventory slot. Steam returns only this way.

powers: Iron Joints (Passive): Defense 18, with no STR requirement.
Boiler Fire (spend 1 Steam): Choose one. A wrist crossbow shot (Free). A hidden blade strike (Action). Advantage on one Might check.
escalation: At 0 Steam the servos lock: Speed 2 and disadvantage on DEX until stoked. If you spend the last Steam in combat, the boilers vent: 1d6 fire to you and everyone adjacent.

name: The Fairy Jar
object: A thumb-high jar of purple glass. Inside, a small furious face swims in mist. The fairy was netted at the Arch of Flowers in Briarheart Forest.
unlock: Learn the fairy's name, which it will not tell you
Promise it freedom, aloud, before a witness
risk: Speak to it before you know its name, and it slips out and hexes you: make a WIL save, DC 12, or have disadvantage on WIL checks for a week.

resource.name: Bargains
resource.text: Bargains (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Bargain per Ask. Regain 1 when you answer the question the fairy asks about its home. It asks one each time it runs dry, and the answer is never found on the way to a gig. Bargains return only this way.

powers: Ask (Action, spend 1 Bargain): Make a WIL save, DC 12. On a success the fairy works one small charm: a glamour, a lock undone, a minute of floating. On a failure it sulks and stays silent for 2d6 days.
Fairy Light (Passive): The jar glows when fey are within 6 spaces.
escalation: On a natural 1 the fairy escapes and curses you. You may smash the jar at any time: it grants +1 to one stat for good and is gone. At 0 Bargains it only bargains for its freedom.

name: The Seven-Leaf Bracelet
object: A silver bracelet of seven linked leaves, cool as morning dew. It was found at the root of the oldest tree in Sunset Grove, and Graysen One-Eye would like to know who took it.
unlock: Wear it through a night in old woods
Answer the first question the trees ask you, truthfully
risk: The trees ask about something you would rather they never knew. Answer truthfully, or the bracelet will not wake until you do. Whatever you answer, every plant in the grove now knows it.

resource.name: Leaves
resource.text: Leaves (finite, 7). Each Listen wilts one leaf. A wilted leaf never comes back, and nothing refills the bracelet.

powers: Listen (Action, spend 1 Leaf): Speak with the plants around you for 10 minutes, or speak Elvish for a day. Plants tell you who passed and may move aside or tangle.
Rustle (Passive): The leaves stir when a creature hiding in or behind plants is within 6 spaces.
escalation: When the last leaf wilts the bracelet buds. Plant it beside a door to elsewhere within a month, and in a year a new bracelet grows there. If you don't plant it, your fingertips start to leaf.

name: The Hexing Needles
object: Three black needles in a felt roll, and a spool of red thread. The roll is stitched in the style of the Sisters of Dusk, the coven that rules Elgrym in Lady Straythe's name.
unlock: Learn the stitch from a witch, at her price
Embroider your own likeness first
risk: Your first stitch slips. You carry a small hex of your own making, and have disadvantage on one kind of roll, the GM's choice, until you unpick it.

resource.name: Thread
resource.text: Thread (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Thread per Stitch. Regain 1 when someone gives you their hair, blood, or cloth freely, knowing what it is for. Thread returns only this way. Unpicking a hex frees its victim but gives back no Thread.

powers: Stitch (an hour of work, spend 1 Thread): Embroider a likeness of someone, using their hair, blood, or cloth. They have disadvantage on one kind of roll you name until the cloth is unpicked or burned. They feel every stitch.
Thread Sense (Passive): You can tell when cloth you touch carries a stitched hex, and whose likeness it is.
escalation: Every victim knows the shape of your hands, and the Sisters of Dusk hear who is stitching in their style. At 0 Thread you can still Stitch, but the hex also lands on your own likeness.

name: The Sown Teeth
object: A hide satchel holding a handful of long dragon teeth from Drakeholm that click together like dice.
unlock: Read the command words etched inside the flap, in a dead language
Sow the first tooth on ground you mean to hold
risk: The first warrior asks whom it must guard. Your answer binds every warrior after it, and the GM holds you to the letter.

resource.name: Teeth
resource.text: Teeth (finite, 1d4+1, rolled at unlock). Each Sow uses up one tooth. A sown tooth never comes back, and nothing refills the satchel.

powers: Sow (Action, spend 1 Tooth): An armored warrior rises from the ground beside you and obeys you for an hour. The GM uses a soldier stat block of your level.
Dragon's Click (Passive): The teeth click louder within 6 spaces of a dragon or dragonkin.
escalation: If two or more warriors stand and one is struck by surprise, they turn on each other, then on whoever is closest. Dragons and their kin can smell the satchel. When the last tooth is gone, the satchel is just a bag.

name: The Arch-Watch Mirror
object: A mirror taller than a man in a frame of blackened ash. Its surface moves like still water. The glass was ground at the Observatory of Infinite Skies.
unlock: Install it in your holding
For each arch it should watch, carry a sliver of its glass through that arch and back, unbroken
risk: Something on the other side sees the mirror before it sees them. Roll a d6 when the last sliver returns: on a 1-2, whatever sees the mirror can look back through it until a night's vigil clears it.

resource.name: Clarity
resource.text: Clarity (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Clarity for Watch or Foresee. Regain all after someone keeps a full night's vigil before the mirror without sleeping. Clarity returns only this way.

powers: Shimmer (Passive): The mirror shimmers whenever a watched arch is used.
Watch (10 minutes, spend 1 Clarity): See a watched arch and the area around it for 10 minutes.
Foresee (spend 1 Clarity, once per episode): Before you go through, ask the GM one question about where the arch leads.
escalation: At 0 Clarity the glass stays clear both ways. Anything beyond a watched arch can look into your holding until the mirror is refilled.

name: The Apology Blade
object: A sword cut from the belly of a sea serpent out of Terrache's cavern sea. It still smells of brine, and its edge is clouded like the sky before a storm.
unlock: Give it as an apology to someone you wronged
If they freely give it back, it wakes
Later: make peace between two who are at war, and its storm wakes
risk: They keep it. Make an Influence check, DC 14, to win it back with a second apology. On a failure the blade is theirs until they choose to return it.

resource.name: Sky
resource.text: Sky (pip tracker, max 3). Spend Sky on Gust and Storm. Regain 1 when someone accepts your apology for a real wrong you did before you took up the blade, or one you did not mean to do. Sky returns only this way.

powers: Overcast (Passive): The clouded edge darkens when a creature within 6 spaces is angry at you over a wrong you have not apologised for.
Gust (Action, spend 1 Sky): A wind throws every creature in a Line 6 back 3 spaces (Knockback 3). STR save, DC 13, negates.
Storm (Action, spend 2 Sky, once the storm wakes): For the encounter, enemies have disadvantage on ranged attacks and you cannot be pushed.
escalation: If you wrong the one who gave it back, it is in their hands the next morning, wherever they are.

name: The Rune Fragment
object: A shard of storm-dark stone veined with silver. One rune on it glows faintly. It was in the hand of an arrival the Archkeepers met, who remembered nothing but its name.
unlock: Find a second fragment
Carve the first rune's name into a gravestone or standing stone, and speak aloud the name of someone who died for something
Hold the fragments together for 10 minutes and they fuse
risk: Whoever carries another fragment feels yours wake. Roll a d6 when they fuse: on a 1-2 the fragments grind against each other and you take 1 Wound.

resource.name: Runes
resource.text: Runes (session-bound, up to 9, one per fused fragment). Each fragment carries one rune, rolled on a d8 when it fuses. Each rune works once, then goes dark. A dark rune relights when you carve it into a gravestone or a standing stone and speak aloud the name of someone who died for something.

powers: Fehu (Action): An item you touch gives +1 to its user for an hour.
Algiz (Free): Advantage on saves against fear and charm for the scene.
Raido (Free): +2 Speed for the scene.
Uruz (Free, after the roll): +2 to a STR check.
Tiwaz (Action): Allies who hear you have advantage on their next attack.
Ansuz (Free): Speak and read any language for a scene.
Eihwaz (Reaction): Reduce one hit's damage by your level plus STR.
Sowilo (Action): Sunlight blinds every enemy within 6 spaces until your next turn. DEX save, DC 13, negates.
escalation: Fragments call to each other, and other holders follow the call. When the ninth fuses, its rune wakes once: change one result, even a past one. Then the stone falls to dust.

name: The Binding Linens
object: Strips of old linen that smell of myrrh, with gold-thread hieroglyphs at the ends. They were taken from the temple dead of Arkus.
unlock: Learn the binding words from a priest of the dead
Wrap and bury a stranger who had no one to bury them
risk: The stranger belonged to someone, and they come asking within a session. Make an Influence check, DC 14, to explain what you did.

resource.name: Strips
resource.text: Strips (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Strip per Hold Back. Regain 1 by preparing and burying someone who has no one to do it for them. Strips return only this way.

powers: Hold Back (Action, spend 1 Strip): Wrap a Dying creature. It stops dying and cannot die from Wounds until it is unwrapped or the next dawn, but it cannot act.
Myrrh (Passive): You know at a glance how long a body has been dead and whether it was ever bound.
escalation: Anyone wrapped a second time comes back a little less. They forget one thing they loved, and the GM chooses what.

name: The Rusted Spear
object: A leaf-bladed spear whose rust never flakes off, however hard you scrub. The Blood Spears of Averost took it from a world they raided, and the watchtower still lists it as unreturned.
unlock: Learn whom it last wounded, and find them
Heal that old wound with the spear's own rust
risk: They remember you and the spear. Make an Influence check, DC 14, to be forgiven. On a failure they hunt for the spear.

resource.name: Rust
resource.text: Rust (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Rust per Scrape. Regain 1 by leaving the spear a night in the red water of Bloodrust Depths. Rust returns only this way.

powers: Spare (Free): When you would drop a creature to 0 HP with the spear, it falls stable instead, and its wound will not close until you choose to mend it.
Scrape (Action, spend 1 Rust): Scrape rust into a wound to heal 1 Wound, or to close a wound the spear made.
escalation: At 0 Rust the blade is clean and bright. The next wound it gives never closes: a hero loses 1 max Wound for good, and a creature bleeds out by the end of the scene.

name: The Derelict Harpoon
object: A ship's harpoon with a coil of glowing strand-line, cut from a derelict hull hung in the vines of Drendaan. The line is warm, and it is still wet.
unlock: Cut a length of strand-line from a derelict hull in Drendaan with the harpoon's own blade
Make one throw that hauls you across a gap you could not have jumped
risk: Whatever lived aboard the hulk feels the line cut. Roll a d6: on a 1-2 it follows the line through the arch within a session.

resource.name: Slack
resource.text: Slack (d6 vs. accumulation). Each time you Haul, roll a d6 against your current Slack, then add 1 Slack. If you roll equal to or below your Slack before adding, the line snarls (see Escalation). Slack clears when you carry a length of the line back to a derelict hull in Drendaan and splice it into the strand.

powers: Haul (Action, Range 12, +1 Slack): Make a ranged attack with the harpoon. On a hit, choose one: pull yourself to the target, or pull a Medium or smaller target up to 6 spaces toward you. A pulled creature falls Prone and can make a STR save, DC 13, to resist.
Anchor (Free, 1/round, after a Haul that hits): Plant the line. The target cannot move more than 6 spaces from you until your next turn or until you let go (Free).
escalation: When the d6 triggers, the line snarls around you or your target, the GM's choice. Both of you are Restrained until someone spends an action to cut it. The cut length keeps glowing, and whatever lived aboard the hulk follows it through the arch.

name: The Seekers' Provenance Ledger
object: A cloth-bound ledger listing a hundred relics by name, maker and rightful owner, in four hands. The last twelve pages are blank and slightly warm. The Museum of Worlds Beyond reports it missing from its archive.
unlock: Return a relic to its rightful owner or their heirs, and have the owner sign it into the ledger
Give up the relic's price: you may not sell it or take payment
risk: The Black Hand hears that someone is naming relics, and the GM starts a six-step Black Hand clock about who.

resource.name: Provenance
resource.text: Provenance (pip tracker, max 3). Spend 1 Provenance per Name the Owner or Vouch. Gain 1 Provenance each time you return a relic to its rightful owner and have them sign it into the ledger. Provenance returns only this way.

powers: Name the Owner (Action, spend 1 Provenance): Touch an object. The ledger writes its maker, its last three owners, and its rightful owner, if it has one. A lie in the record shows as an ink blot.
Vouch (Reaction, spend 1 Provenance): When an ally within 6 spaces makes an Influence check about an object or its owner, they have advantage.
Margins (Passive): The ledger shows a blot when you hold it within 6 spaces of a stolen or cursed object.
escalation: When the last Provenance is spent, the ledger writes one relic's name and its rightful owner on a blank page without being asked. The GM chooses the relic, and the owner is someone you know. The Seekers of the Sun and the Black Hand both learn it has been written.

name: The Black Goat's Tally-Stick
object: A notched black-wood stick as long as a hand, each notch a tab paid or unpaid at the Black Goat's Tavern. A horned goat's single yellow eye is burned into one end.
unlock: Drink at the Black Goat's Tavern through a full night, and settle your tab in full
Broker a meeting there between two parties who would fight anywhere else, and keep it peaceful
risk: If a peace you broker at the tavern breaks, you take 1 Wound along with the one who broke it.

resource.name: Truce
resource.text: Truce (toggle, on/off). Strike the stick on a table to call a Truce, which turns it on. It turns off when the parley ends, when you end it, or when anyone attempts violence under it. Once off, it cannot be turned on again until you have brokered a meeting between two enemies who would not otherwise have met, and settled the tab for it at the Black Goat's Tavern.

powers: Call a Truce (Action, turn Truce on): Name a place and up to six people in it. For an hour, or until the parley ends, a named creature that tries to attack another named creature makes a WIL save, DC 14. On a failure the attack does not happen and the Truce ends.
Read the Notches (Passive): When you hold the stick at a table, you know who in the room owes whom, and whether the debt is money, a favor, or blood.
escalation: If the Truce breaks, the stick burns your palm for 1 Wound, and the Black Goat's wardens come for whoever broke it within a session. Vynan Halfhorn will want to know why the peace failed under his stick.
